design.objective: Project detail requests use their route project ID without changing the global project selector.
users: Project members opening a detail project while the global selector targets another accessible project.

requirements.statement: Keep a project-detail route target independent from the global project selector.
acceptance: Every /api/project/{projectId} request sends that path ID as X-Project-Id.
Opening or editing a project detail does not change the stored global selector.
The server path/header consistency check remains enforced.
counterexample: A basic-information save uses the global selector project ID.
Entering a detail route changes the selector.

invariants: The global selector changes only through an explicit selector action.
Server-side path/header, authorization, tenant, entity, audit and lock checks remain intact.
constraints: Only current task writable paths may change.
Do not modify http.ts, project-context store, backend security, database or API payloads.

selected_approach.name: Explicit per-request project context
selected_approach.reason: It reuses the existing request configuration and limits change to project detail API clients.

alternatives.name: Infer context in the common HTTP interceptor
alternatives.rejected_because: Expands impact to a global public client.

components.name: Project API clients
components.responsibility: Bind project request context to the path project ID

data_flows.input: Global selector A and detail route B
data_flows.output: B is editable and A persists globally.

compatibility: Preserve paths, methods, bodies and global selector state
operations: No migration or deployment configuration change

verification_strategy.signal: Header and route IDs match while selector remains different
verification_strategy.method: Vite build, static API inspection and local browser A/B scenario.

assumptions.text: withProjectContext takes precedence over stored global context.
assumptions.basis: Existing HTTP interceptor checks explicit projectContext before local storage.
assumptions.falsifier: Browser request header remains the global selector ID.

decisions.decision: Use route project ID for every project-detail API request without selector synchronization.
decisions.reason: Fix stale global context rejection while preserving security.

risks.impact: That action still fails with stale global selection
risks.mitigation: Audit all project path API functions and validate A/B browser paths.

global_constraints: Do not mutate global project selection.
Do not modify common HTTP, store, backend or database files.
